Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a short spreadsheet that lists the categories of PII MedSys expects to send to Redwood for our real-time summarization integration (MedSys_PIIScope.xlsx). Before we proceed with onboarding we'd like to confirm the following so our legal and compliance teams can complete their review: 

- A high-level data flow diagram showing where PII is stored, where inference happens, and any cross-border movements.
- An access matrix: which Redwood roles have access to identifiable data, and controls for engineers vs. SREs vs. support.
- Subprocessor list and cadence for disclosure (how do we get notified of changes?).
- Encryption at rest and in transit details, including KMS type and key custody.
- Retention and deletion guarantees for request-level logs and KV caches.

Can you send a preliminary data flow diagram and an access matrix by next Tuesday (Mar 2)? Also flag any items you think require a DPA amendment. We can schedule a short sync once you share the artifacts.

Evelyn / Marcus — leaving notes from legal review of the questionnaire and a draft access matrix attached (Redwood_PII_Access_Matrix_v0.2.xlsx). Key items we should confirm before sending to MedSys: 

1) Retention: our standard is 30 days for request payloads used for debugging, unless customer requests shorter retention. We can offer configurable retention in Dedicated/Private. Need to confirm whether MedSys requires deletion-on-request for inference logs sooner.

2) Subprocessors: we publish a running list monthly. For DPA purposes, legal prefers to include a sentence about 30-day notification for material subprocessor additions, and immediate notice for subprocessors that will process PII. Confirm operationally if that cadence is feasible.

3) Cross-border flows: if MedSys requires EU-only processing, Redwood Private or a dedicated EU deployment is the recommended path. For Hosted, we currently process in us-east-1 for their region unless otherwise requested.

4) De-identification: we should offer an optional post-processing step that strips high-risk PII (SSNs, medical record numbers) before logs are stored — Marcus, can you indicate if we can provide that as an opt-in pipeline?

Once Marcus confirms items 1/4 and provides the KMS + storage details, I’ll draft suggested DPA redlines and a short cover note for Sarah.

-Neha
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Neha / Evelyn — technical confirmations below (short bullets, to cut to the chase):

- Hosting: hosted inference currently runs in AWS us-east-1 for this sales region. Dedicated/EU options are available per contract.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; all persisted objects encrypted at rest using AWS KMS. Customer-managed CMKs supported in Dedicated/Private (bring-your-own-key).
- Key custody: Hosted default uses Redwood-managed CMKs; can offer customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private.
- Log retention: Request-level logs are stored encrypted in S3 with lifecycle policies; default 30d but configurable. KV caches are ephemeral in GPU memory, not persisted beyond container lifetime unless debug mode enabled.
- Access controls: Role-based access via IAM + RBAC in the console. Support engineers do not have automatic access to customer plaintext; access requires an audited escalation workflow.
- De-identification: We can insert an opt-in post-processing step before writing logs that redacts regex-defined identifiers (SSN, MRN, email). This is a configuration change but feasible for MedSys with a small implementation effort (~2-3 engineering days).

I updated the data flow diagram to include S3 buckets, KMS arrows, and the optional de-id pipeline. I’ve uploaded an internal diagram to the MedSys onboarding folder (link below).

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMedSysOnboarding

-Marcus
Principal Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for your patience. Attached are the artefacts we discussed: an updated data flow diagram and our access matrix. Below are concise answers to your original checklist; I’ve included inline notes where you asked for DPA-impacting items.

Attachments included: Redwood_DFDiagram_v1.1.png, Redwood_PII_Access_Matrix_v0.2.xlsx

Summary answers (high level):
- Data flow: inference occurs in-host (us-east-1 by default). Temporary KV caches exist in RAM for session context and are not persisted unless debug mode is explicitly enabled. Persisted request logs are encrypted in S3; we can set lifecycle to your requested retention. See attached diagram for KMS and S3 locations.
- Encryption & KMS: TLS in transit; AWS KMS for at-rest. Hosted default uses Redwood-managed CMKs; we can support customer-managed CMKs for Dedicated/Private. DPA note: we recommend an explicit clause allowing customer-managed keys for regulated workloads.
- Access matrix: engineers have scoped, audited access via RBAC; support access requires an internal approval workflow and is logged. See attached matrix for role-by-role permissions.
- Subprocessor notifications: we publish a monthly list; for material additions that process PII we will provide 30-day notice and immediate notice for changes with direct processing impact. Legal will propose a sentence for the DPA.
- De-identification: We can enable an opt-in regex-driven redaction pipeline prior to persistence — this is configurable and we estimate a 2-3 day engineering effort to enable for MedSys.

Next steps:
1) Neha will provide DPA redline suggestions for the customer-managed keys and notifications language.
2) Marcus will collaborate with your engineering team if you want the opt-in de-id pipeline.
3) Propose 30-min sync to confirm retention window and whether MedSys requires EU-only processing (if so we’ll scope Dedicated/Private options). Please let us know availability this week.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
